- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent high.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of past 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–2%.
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and price is falling, model often ignores trend reversal; add 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid false continuation bias.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid false bottom bias.
- Model tends to overestimate in periods with high volatility; apply volatility-adjusted downward correction (e.g., -0.5% per 10% standard deviation in recent 7-day range).
